Mighty Men
MY-tee men
noun
From mighty + men; the valiant warriors of David, and the term for men of valour in Scripture.

📖 Biblical Definition

The mighty men were the valiant warriors gathered about David, his band of heroes whose exploits are recorded in the books of Samuel and Chronicles. They came to him first in the cave of Adullam, when every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented gathered to him, and he became a captain over them; and out of that desperate company the LORD made an army of mighty men. The chief of them—Adino, Eleazar, Shammah, and the rest—did valiant deeds: one slew eight hundred at one time, another held a plot of ground against the Philistines when the people fled, another smote a lion in a pit on a snowy day. Three of them broke through the host of the Philistines to draw water from the well of Bethlehem at David’s longing, but David would not drink it, pouring it out unto the LORD, for it was the blood of men who had jeoparded their lives. The mighty men are a picture of what grace makes of the broken and the desperate: gathered to the LORD’s anointed in their distress, they are transformed into valiant warriors, bound to their captain in loyal love, and made the instruments of his victories. The dictionary honors the mighty men of David as a type of the soldiers of Christ, the true Son of David, who gathers the distressed and the indebted to Himself and makes of them, by grace, mighty men of valour in His warfare.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The valiant warriors of David, gathered from the distressed and indebted at Adullam; a picture of what grace makes of the broken—mighty men bound to the LORD’s anointed.

expand to see more

MIGHTY MEN, the valiant warriors gathered about David.

They came to him at Adullam: the distressed, the indebted, the discontented.

Their chiefs did valiant deeds against the Philistines and others.

Three broke through the host to fetch water from Bethlehem’s well.

A picture of grace transforming the broken into men of valour.

📖 Key Scripture

1Sa 22:2 — "And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men."

2Sa 23:8 — "These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time."

2Sa 23:16 — "And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the LORD."

1Ch 12:18 — "Then the spirit came upon Amasai, who was chief of the captains, and he said, Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: Peace, peace be unto thee, and peace be to thine helpers; for thy God helpeth thee. Then David received them, and made them captains of the band."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The mighty men are reduced to mere military legend; Scripture sets them as a picture of grace transforming the broken into valiant servants of the LORD’s anointed.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the reduction of the mighty men to mere military legend—a heroic muster-roll of ancient warriors with no spiritual significance. But Scripture frames them as a work of grace. They came to David not as polished soldiers but as the distressed, the indebted, the discontented (1 Sam 22:2), a desperate company gathered to the LORD’s rejected anointed in the cave; and out of that company the LORD made an army of valiant men.

The principle to recover is what grace makes of the broken who gather to the LORD’s anointed. The mighty men were bound to David in loyal love—Thine are we, David, and on thy side, for thy God helpeth thee (1 Chr 12:18)—and their valour flowed from that allegiance. They jeoparded their lives for him; he poured out their costly gift unto the LORD (2 Sam 23:16). So they are a type of the soldiers of Christ, the true Son of David, who gathers the distressed and indebted to Himself in their need and makes of them, by His grace, mighty men of valour in His warfare. The desperate who come to Him are not left as they were; grace transforms them into faithful servants.
